title: A familiar forked bone
hook: Some fossil and living skeletons share a structure.

knows: Birds and other theropods can be compared by skeletal anatomy.
doesNotKnow: Recognize a furcula in two stipulated anatomical examples.

misconception: A wishbone is found only in living birds.
objective: Recognize a furcula in two stipulated anatomical examples.

claims.text: Some fossil and living skeletons share a structure. A bird and an identified non-avian theropod specimen both have a furcula. What shape is being compared in this schematic? Both schematic chest views highlight a forked furcula, or wishbone, near the shoulders and ribs. A shared structure can contribute to anatomical comparison; these simplified drawings do not show the full skeleton or establish how either animal moved.

claims.text: The figure uses simplified, not-to-scale front chest views. Only schematic shoulder points, ribs and a highlighted furcula are shown; it is not an image or full skeletal reconstruction of an identified specimen.
Recall: What is another name for the forked furcula? Furcula is another name for the wishbone.
